---
name: pcb-design
description: Edit a KiCad 10 board project with native schematic edits, check it with ERC, DRC, simulation and export checks, and prepare a neutral manufacturing export. Use for RC and small bare-board designs. Not for SKiDL circuits.
---

# pcb-design

This skill guides an agent through a KiCad board design. The agent designs and edits the circuit.
The script `scripts/pcb.py` checks the project and runs the tools. The script never designs a circuit.

## Scope

| Route | Status |
|---|---|
| Native schematic (`${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_sch`) with six measured edit kinds: value, add part, remove part, footprint, reorder, no edit | Supported. See `references/native-edit.md`. |
| SKiDL generated schematic | Refused. `source.skidl_unsupported`, exit 2. |
| Netlist import, IPC API, pcbnew updater | Not used. `pcbnew` only reads the board. |
| GUI update adapter (`update --adapter gui`) | Supported for KiCad 10.0.5 in the runtime image, with one measured dialog layout. See `references/gui-update.md`. |

Open limits: one measured fixture, one machine, KiCad 10.0.5 only, no supplier qualification, no zone refill inside a GUI update.

## Procedure

1. Read `references/design-workflow.md`. It lists the decisions and the check that closes each one.
2. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py env --project PROJECT`. Stop if the report does not show the lock image.
3. Edit the schematic as described in `references/native-edit.md`. Write the expected-difference file before the edit.
4. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py erc --project PROJECT`. Repair each unwaived violation.
5. Update the board from the schematic with `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project PROJECT --adapter gui --expect FILE`. `FILE` is the identity expectation that you wrote before the edit (see `references/gui-update.md`). Use the manual route for any other board edit, and follow `references/placement-routing.md`.
6. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py drc --project PROJECT` (add `--refill-zones` to refill the zones and save the board).
7. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py sim --project PROJECT` when `${PROJECT}/simulations/` exists.
8. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py interface --project PROJECT --apply --expect out/reports/update.expect.json` after a GUI update, settings or refill change that the wrapper made. Otherwise record a review with `interface --record-review`.
9. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py export --project PROJECT` after clean ERC and DRC results.
10. Run `uv run scripts/pcb.py check --project PROJECT --for ready`. Report the exit code and the state.

Run every command from the skill directory, or give the absolute path to `scripts/pcb.py`.

## Rules for the agent

- Never edit a hash by hand, for example `board_sha256` in `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json` or a waiver hash. A hand edit gives an `interface.review_stale` or `interface.geometry_stale` finding (exit 1). Run the command that owns the hash instead.
- Before you edit `kicad/board.kicad_pcb` by hand, run `uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project ${PROJECT} --adapter manual`. It preserves the prior board. It exits 2 by design. Then edit the board. Without the preserved board, the rebinding of the interface is refused.

- Keep the symbol UUID and the `instances` path of each existing symbol. Never delete and re-add a part to change it.
- Change a footprint only through its `Footprint` property.
- Never move a symbol to another sheet. The identity is lost.
- A board change makes every ERC waiver stale. No operation renews a waiver. The user must renew the waivers.
- A GUI save by the user has no prior copy. The rebinding of the interface is then refused. Use the review record.
- Do not claim that a board is ready when `check --for ready` exits 1.
- Do not claim an identity-kept change when the identity comparison shows an unexpected difference.

## Records

`${PROJECT}/manufacturing/supplier.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/export.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/waivers.yaml`, `board.yaml`, `variants.yaml`, `${PROJECT}/components/part.yaml`, `toolchain.lock.json`, `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json` and `${PROJECT}/mechanical/interface-review.json` are records. `scripts/validate.py` checks them. The schemas are in `contracts/schemas/`. Run `uv run scripts/validate.py --schemas contracts/schemas --project PROJECT` to check the records alone.

## Waivers

A waiver lists the exact KiCad item UUIDs of one finding. The set of UUIDs must equal the set of the finding. A label is for display only. A UUID that occurs two times in the project cannot be waived. A waiver for another board or revision is stale and fails the check.

## Exit codes

See `references/exit-codes.md`. The precedence is 3, then 2, then 1, then 0.

## Runtime

See `references/runtime.md`. The container image is the only supported runtime in this version. The lock names the image and its ID. A different ID is a refusal.

## Files

- `scripts/pcb.py`: the commands.
- `scripts/board_inventory.py`: the pcbnew worker that reads holes and placement in the container.
- `scripts/validate.py`, `scripts/project_io.py`, `scripts/identity.py`, `scripts/sexp.py`: accepted helpers. They are copies and do not change.
- `contracts/`: the record schemas and the copy of their README.
- `runtime/`: the fixed build recipe.
- `templates/rc-bare-board/`: a bare RC board project.
- `examples/rc-edit/`: one value edit with its before files, after files and expected difference.

# Design workflow

Each decision has a place where it is recorded and a check that closes it.

| # | Decision | Recorded in | Closed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Requirements and board statement | `board.yaml` (`restrictions`, `electrical_limits`) | `check` (record validation) |
| 2 | Circuit topology and values | `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_sch` | `erc` (no unwaived violation) |
| 3 | Datasheet and pin-to-pad map | `${PROJECT}/components/part.yaml` (`pin_map`, `datasheet_url`) | `check` (part record validation) |
| 4 | Power budget | `board.yaml` `electrical_limits` and a hand calculation | Reviewer note in `${PROJECT}/docs/` |
| 5 | Simulated response | `${PROJECT}/simulations/*.cir` and `${PROJECT}/simulations/assertions.json` | `sim` (each assertion within tolerance) |
| 6 | Footprints and placement | `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_pcb` | `drc` (with schematic parity) |
| 7 | Routing and copper | `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_pcb` | `drc` (no unwaived violation) |
| 8 | Zone fill | `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_pcb` | `drc --refill-zones` (the board is saved) |
| 9 | Decoupling and return path | `${PROJECT}/docs/layout-notes.md` | Reviewer note |
| 10 | Interface geometry | `${PROJECT}/mechanical/board-interface.json` | `interface --apply` or `interface --record-review` |
| 11 | Waivers | `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/waivers.yaml` | `erc` and `drc` (exact UUID match) |
| 12 | Supplier limits | `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/supplier.yaml` | `check` (record validation) |
| 13 | Export contract | `${PROJECT}/manufacturing/export.yaml` | `export` (seven checks) |
| 14 | Plot settings | Saved board (`pcbplotparams`) | `settings` |
| 15 | Toolchain | `toolchain.lock.json` | `env` (image ID equals the lock) |
| 16 | Release revision | `board.yaml` `release_revision` | `check` (waiver and interface revision match) |
| 17 | Ready state | `${PROJECT}/out/reports/*.result.json` | `check --for ready` |

Do the decisions in this order. Each change to the board stales the results that depend on it.
# Native schematic edits

Edit `${PROJECT}/kicad/board.kicad_sch` as text. Keep the file a valid KiCad 10 schematic.

## Measured edit kinds

| Kind | Supported | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Value | Yes | Change the `Value` property of the symbol. Keep the UUID. |
| Add part | Yes | A new symbol gets a new UUID. Its `instances` path uses the same root as the other symbols. |
| Remove part | Yes | Remove the whole symbol and its wires. Record the removed UUID in the expected-difference file. |
| Footprint | Yes | Change the `Footprint` property only. Do not change the footprint UUID by delete and re-add. |
| Reorder | Yes | Change the order of the symbols in the file. The UUIDs stay. |
| No edit | Yes | Used as the control case. |

The replace-off run is an option experiment. It is not a supported edit kind.

## Rules

- Keep the symbol UUID and the `instances` path of each existing symbol.
- Never move a symbol to another sheet. The identity is lost and a duplicate is added.
- Never delete and re-add a part to change it. The new footprint has a new UUID and a default position.
- Write the expected-difference file before the edit. Use the `identity.py` format: `{"differences": [{"op", "class", "ident", "field", "before", "after"}]}`. Write raw values for `before` and `after`.
- After the edit, run `uv run --no-project --no-config python scripts/identity.py snapshot` on the board before and after the board edit, then `compare --expect`.
- A changed or removed track needs a UUID entry in the expected-difference file.
- Run `erc` after each schematic edit.

## Example

See `examples/rc-edit/`. It changes the value of R2 from 10k to 20k. The file `expected-difference.json` lists the one expected change.

# GUI update and the manual route

## Manual route (default)

`uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project PROJECT --adapter manual` does three things:

1. It preserves the current board in `${PROJECT}/out/history/boards/`.
2. It writes the handoff file `${PROJECT}/out/handoff/manual.json` with the input hashes and the pending step.
3. It exits 2 with `update.manual_required`. The dependent steps stop.

The user or the agent then saves the board in KiCad. Next, run `drc` (for parity) and examine the interface. A board saved by KiCad has no automatic rebinding proof. Record the review with `interface --record-review`.

## GUI adapter

`uv run scripts/pcb.py update --project PROJECT --adapter gui --expect FILE [--replace on|off] [--delete on|off] [--relink on|off]`

Write `FILE` before the update. It has the identity format (`{"differences": [...]}`) and lists each change that the schematic update may cause. Each entry uses raw `before` and `after` values.

The adapter runs in the runtime image on a staged copy of the project. It does this in order:

1. Preflight. The image must match the lock. KiCad must be 10.0.5. Xvfb, xdotool, ImageMagick `import` and `kicad` must exist. Otherwise the command exits 2 with `update.adapter_unavailable`.
2. It starts KiCad in Xvfb at 1600x1000, opens the update dialog, sets the three options, updates the PCB, saves the board and closes KiCad.
3. It measures the option states and the KiCad exit. The KiCad exit must be `exited` with code 0. A different option state exits 3 with `update.option_mismatch`.
4. It compares the saved board with `FILE` by the identity reader. A difference that `FILE` does not list exits 1 with `update.identity_mismatch`. Nothing is published.
5. It runs DRC with schematic parity. Any parity finding exits 1 with `update.parity`. Other DRC diagnostics are recorded, and the state is `not_ready`.
6. It checks the whole board with the three allowed normalizations (section 13 of the proposal). Then it preserves the prior board, writes the board, and records the change. Then run `interface --apply --expect out/reports/update.expect.json`.

Limits: one dialog layout (KiCad 10.0.5, screen 1600x1000, no window manager). The option states are read from screen pixels. A zone refill is not part of a GUI update.
